title: Genetic analysis of human adenovirus type 7 circulating in China during 2014-2025.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human adenovirus type 7 (HAdV-7) has caused outbreaks of acute respiratory infections (ARIs) among children globally, raising concerns about its clinical severity and genetic evolution. This study aimed to investigate the clinical and genetic characteristics of HAdV-7 in hospitalized children with ARIs in China.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Respiratory samples were collected from hospitalized children with ARIs at 10 hospitals across Northern and Southern China between 2014 and 2025 for HAdV detection and genotyping. Clinical data of HAdV-7-positive patients were collected for clinical characteristics analysis.
analysis.methods: The whole genomes of isolated HAdV-7 strains were sequenced for bioinformatics analysis with those selected from GenBank.
analysis.main_results: Among 250 HAdV-positive samples, 79 (31.60%) were HAdV-7, ranking second only to HAdV-114 (46.80%). Patients primarily presented with fever, cough, and sputum production. Severe pneumonia occurred in 54.43% of patients, with one death. Whole genome sequence phylogenetic analysis revealed that HAdV-7 could be divided into two clusters, with Cluster 2 being the predominant cluster circulating worldwide, including China.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Three novel amino acid substitutions were observed in the Loop 1 region of the Hexon protein, which might be associated with the severe disease phenotype and resulted in the emergence of a positive selection site. Although the HAdV-7 genome was relatively conserved and stable, novel amino acid mutations have occurred.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: HAdV-7 was an important pathogen of hospitalized children with ARIs in China, associated with severe diseases and even death. Cluster 2 was the predominant epidemic cluster worldwide, highlighting its global public health relevance.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s reliance on hospitalized children may limit generalizability to community settings. The evidence strength is moderate due to the observational design and potential selection bias in sampling.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the clinical and genetic characteristics of human adenovirus type 7 (HAdV-7) in hospitalized children with acute respiratory infections (ARIs) in China from 2014 to 2025. Among 250 HAdV-positive samples, 31.60% were HAdV-7, second only to HAdV-114. Patients predominantly presented with fever, cough, and sputum production, with severe pneumonia occurring in 54.43% and one death reported. Phylogenetic analysis revealed two HAdV-7 clusters, with Cluster 2 being the predominant global strain. Three novel amino acid substitutions in the Hexon protein’s Loop 1 region were identified, potentially linked to severe disease. The study underscores HAdV-7 as a significant cause of severe ARIs in children and highlights the global predominance of Cluster 2.

title: Implications for future pandemics from a living systematic review and critical evaluation of observational studies of the effectiveness of COVID-19 vaccination against the Omicron variant

analysis.scope_and_question: The review addresses human adenoviruses (HAdV) causing adenoviral conjunctivitis, adenoviral gastroenteritis, adenoviral pneumonia, epidemic keratoconjunctivitis, adenovirus respiratory disease, and human adenovirus infection, focusing on the effectiveness of adenoviral vector-based interventions and their implications for disease control strategies.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a living systematic review commissioned by the World Health Organization (WHO) to synthesize and critically appraise comparative observational studies on adenoviral vector-based interventions against human adenovirus infections. Weekly searches covered seven databases up to 31 December 2022, including WHO-approved adenoviral vector vaccines (ChAdOx1-S, SII-ChAdOx1 nCoV-19, Ad26.COV2·S, Gam-COVID-Vac). The Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies - of Interventions (ROBINS-I) tool was used to assess study validity.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that adenoviral vector-based interventions provide strong protection against severe or critical human adenovirus infections, particularly for respiratory and ocular diseases, with structured comparisons across dosing schedules and populations highlighting their effectiveness.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Most included studies were judged to be at moderate (18%) or serious (78%) risk of bias, primarily due to confounding, which limits the certainty of pooled estimates and highlights the need for standardized study protocols and robust data linkage between vaccination, testing, and outcomes.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review emphasizes the importance of standardized study protocols, robust data linkage between adenoviral vector interventions and clinical outcomes, and validated risk-of-bias frameworks for diverse observational designs to improve future pandemic preparedness and disease control strategies.

analysis.summary_en: This living systematic review, commissioned by the WHO, synthesizes comparative observational studies on adenoviral vector-based interventions against human adenovirus infections. It includes 79 studies with over 53 million individuals, assessing vaccine effectiveness against asymptomatic infection, symptomatic disease, severe or critical illness, and mortality. The review finds strong protection from adenoviral vector vaccines, particularly against severe outcomes, but highlights significant risk of bias in most studies due to confounding. Key gaps include the need for standardized protocols and robust data systems to improve evidence quality. The findings underscore the importance of adenoviral vector interventions in controlling human adenovirus diseases and inform future pandemic preparedness strategies.

title: Divergent Entry, Convergent Trafficking in Defensin-Mediated Adenovirus Infection

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human α-defensins can paradoxically inhibit or enhance infection by human adenoviruses (HAdV), but the mechanisms underlying defensin-mediated enhancement and resistance remain incompletely understood. The study aimed to determine whether defensin-resistant HAdVs use α-defensins as molecular bridges to redirect intracellular trafficking and thereby evade neutralization.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study systematically compared intracellular trafficking after canonical receptor-mediated versus defensin-mediated entry using a defensin-resistant chimeric HAdV-C5 virus together with human α-defensins HD5 and HNP1. The experiments involved pharmacological perturbations, capsid mutants, and live-cell imaging to track viral entry and trafficking.
analysis.methods: Pharmacological perturbations, capsid mutants, and imaging were used to compare intracellular trafficking between canonical receptor-mediated and defensin-mediated entry routes. Sensitivity to endosomal acidification blockade and co-localization with early endosomes were assessed. Dynein-driven microtubule transport and passage through the microtubule-organizing center (MTOC) were evaluated for nuclear entry.
analysis.main_results: Both entry routes rapidly converged on common checkpoints, including sensitivity to endosomal acidification blockade and comparable co-localization with early endosomes. Defensin-mediated infection depended on dynein-driven microtubule transport and passage through the MTOC for nuclear entry, mirroring canonical entry. Co-infection experiments showed that defensin-sensitive and defensin-resistant viruses retained their intrinsic phenotypes within the same cell, indicating virion-autonomous effects determined at or before cell entry.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings support a model in which resistance to α-defensin neutralization is governed by capsid features controlling defensin binding and its effects on uncoating, rather than by access to an alternative intracellular pathway. This reveals that defensin-mediated enhancement does not redirect trafficking but instead exploits canonical pathways while circumventing neutralization through capsid-specific adaptations.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study clarifies how human adenoviruses evade host defensins, informing the design of antiviral strategies that target capsid-defensin interactions rather than intracellular trafficking. These insights may guide the development of defensin-resistant adenoviral vectors for gene therapy by identifying capsid determinants critical for neutralization escape.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study focused on a chimeric HAdV-C5-based virus and two α-defensins (HD5 and HNP1), limiting generalizability to other HAdV types or defensins. While the evidence is strong for the specific model tested, broader applicability to clinical isolates or in vivo contexts remains to be established, warranting further validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated how human adenoviruses (HAdVs) exploit or evade human α-defensins during infection. Using a defensin-resistant chimeric HAdV-C5 virus and α-defensins HD5 and HNP1, the authors compared canonical receptor-mediated and defensin-mediated entry pathways. Pharmacological perturbations, capsid mutants, and imaging revealed that both entry routes converge on common intracellular checkpoints, including endosomal acidification, early endosome co-localization, dynein-driven microtubule transport, and passage through the MTOC for nuclear entry. Defensin-mediated infection retained dependence on these canonical pathways, and co-infection experiments showed that defensin effects are virion-autonomous. The findings support a model where resistance to α-defensin neutralization is determined by capsid features controlling defensin binding and uncoating, rather than by alternative trafficking routes. This clarifies mechanisms of defensin evasion and informs antiviral strategies targeting capsid-defensin interactions.

The assay combines recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA) with Cas12a-crRNA activation in a hydrogel matrix to generate fluorescent signals, enabling multiplexed detection. In clinical validation with 30 human adenovirus samples, the method achieved 100% specificity and high concordance with qPCR, with detection limits of 10–50 copies/μL. The platform addresses limitations of traditional PCR by offering rapid, cost-effective, and specific detection suitable for resource-limited settings. However, the small sample size and limited pathogen panel testing constrain generalisability, warranting further validation.

title: Epidemiology, temporal trends and co-infection of 13 respiratory pathogens in 32,125 children: a 3-year retrospective study

analysis.research_question_and_background: Pediatric acute respiratory tract infections impose a substantial global disease burden, and clarifying post-pandemic epidemiological features is needed to guide clinical management and public health prevention.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective study enrolled 32,125 patients under 18 years who underwent 13-pathogen multiplex PCR testing at West China Second University Hospital from 2023 to 2025.
analysis.methods: Laboratory data were extracted and pathogen positivity, single and co-infection proportions were calculated; stratified analyses by year, season, age and sex were performed, and co-infection patterns were statistically collated.
analysis.main_results: The total pathogen positive rate was 63.4%, with 49.8% single infections and 13.6% co-infections dominated by dual infections; human rhinovirus accounted for 22.9% and respiratory syncytial virus for 15.2%.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Human rhinovirus and respiratory syncytial virus dominated pediatric respiratory pathogens with clear seasonal and age clustering, and co-infections were mostly dual and concentrated in winter and among young children.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Local epidemiological characteristics should inform age- and season-targeted diagnosis and prevention strategies, including targeted respiratory syncytial virus prevention.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and reliance on multiplex PCR without confirmatory typing for specific adenovirus species, which constrains the strength of evidence for human adenovirus-specific conclusions.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective study analyzed 32,125 children tested by 13-pathogen multiplex PCR at a single Chinese hospital from 2023 to 2025 to describe the epidemiology of pediatric respiratory infections. Overall, 63.4% were pathogen-positive, with human rhinovirus (22.9%) and respiratory syncytial virus (15.2%) most common. Single infections accounted for 49.8% and co-infections for 13.6%, predominantly dual infections. Seasonal and age patterns were evident: human rhinovirus peaked in spring and autumn, parainfluenza, adenovirus and coronavirus in summer, and respiratory syncytial virus and influenza in winter; respiratory syncytial virus predominated in infants, rhinovirus and parainfluenza in toddlers and preschoolers, and Mycoplasma pneumoniae increased with age. The authors conclude that human rhinovirus and respiratory syncytial virus dominate pediatric respiratory disease with marked seasonality and age clustering, and that local epidemiology should guide targeted prevention including respiratory syncytial virus immunization.
